tasks.prompt: You are working in the lfc-bot repository: a Discord bot for trading Magic: The Gathering cards. Listings are marked terminal via two service functions in src/services/listings.ts: fulfillListing(id) and softDeleteListing(id), both implemented through a shared setStatus(id, status) helper. There is a bug: setStatus updates the listing's status by id alone, with no check on the listing's CURRENT status - it runs db.update(listings).set({ status, updatedAt: now() }).where(eq(listings.id, id)).run(). This means a listing that is already 'fulfilled', 'deleted', or 'expired' can be fulfilled or deleted again, silently resurrecting it. The command handlers (fulfill.ts, delete.ts, admin/remove.ts) only check listing ownership or server membership, never the listing's current status, so this reaches production behavior directly. Implement the fix and update the matching test coverage in tests/services/listings.test.ts. Requirements: (1) setStatus (and therefore fulfillListing and softDeleteListing) must only change a listing's status when its CURRENT status is 'active' - calling fulfillListing or softDeleteListing on a listing whose status is already 'fulfilled', 'deleted', or 'expired' must leave its status unchanged. (2) Calling fulfillListing or softDeleteListing on a genuinely active listing must still work exactly as before. (3) Add test coverage in tests/services/listings.test.ts proving this: seed a listing, call softDeleteListing on it once, then call fulfillListing on the same id and assert its status is still 'deleted', not 'fulfilled' (and the symmetric fulfill-then-delete case). (4) Your new test must FAIL if only your setStatus fix is reverted while the test stays - it must genuinely depend on the fix, not pass regardless. Change ONLY these two files: src/services/listings.ts and tests/services/listings.test.ts. Do not commit. Do not touch any other file, including the command handlers. When done, run `npx vitest run tests/services/listings.test.ts` and make sure it passes.

The number is parsed by looking the captured word up in a word-to-number map (NUMBER_WORDS, covering 'one' through 'twelve'). tasks.prompt: You are working in the ASoHaVCompanionApp repository (A Story of Heroes and Villains): a tabletop companion app with a Content Admin panel for editing the shared game library (glossary, moves, clocks, etc). apps/server/src/routes/library.ts has seven write routes (create, update, delete, settings, import, reset, restore) that each do two things in sequence: first call saveLibrary(...) to persist the change, then call appendChangeLog(...) to record an audit-log entry. These are two separate, non-transactional database calls, and the save always happens first. There is a bug: if appendChangeLog throws (for any reason - a schema mismatch, a transient DB error, anything), the route lets that exception propagate and reports the whole request as failed with a 5xx - even though the actual library write already succeeded and is fully committed. An admin who sees a failure response for a write that actually landed has no correct next move: retrying re-applies a change that already happened, and assuming nothing saved is simply wrong. Fix this so a failure in the audit-log append is reported as a WARNING alongside a successful response, never as a failed request - the response should still indicate success (its normal shape/status), but carry an additional optional field (e.g. warning: string) noting that the audit entry could not be written, while the underlying error is still logged server-side (e.g. via console.error) so it isn't silently swallowed. This must apply to all seven write routes (create, update, delete, settings, import, reset, restore). A route call where the audit log succeeds must behave exactly as before (no warning field, or an undefined/absent one). Add or update tests in library.test.ts proving: for each of the seven routes, if appendChangeLog throws, the response still reports the underlying operation's normal success status (not a 5xx) and includes a warning noting the audit failure, AND that saveLibrary was actually called (the write really happened) before the warning path is reached; and that no warning field appears when the audit log succeeds normally. Your added/updated test(s) must FAIL if only your route-handling fix is reverted while the test changes stay. Change ONLY these two files: apps/server/src/routes/library.ts and apps/server/src/routes/library.test.ts. Do not commit. Do not touch any other file (in particular, do not touch any frontend/web files - this task is server-only). tasks.prompt: You are working in the ASoHaVCompanionApp repository. apps/server/src/repo.ts's appendChangeLog function inserts a new row into the 'changelog' table via a Supabase client call, and currently generates its own id for that row using a helper (newId('log')) that produces a string like 'log-2mks435g'.
